body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across the 82 live contracts pulled from Kalshi and Polymarket. That's not unusual for gold trackers — it just means no order-book mismatch was large enough, after fees, to lock in a riskless profit right now.

The price backdrop explains why the books look the way they do. Gold has been on a strong run, with one tracker showing gold rose to 4,350.36 USD/t.oz on September 11, 2026, up 0.76% from the previous day, and noting the metal is still 19.41% higher than a year ago. A same-day price check put spot near $4,371 per ounce... a $120 decrease compared to the same time yesterday, underscoring how choppy the metal has been intraday. That volatility shows up directly in the contract pricing: Kalshi's September 30 settle above ladder crosses 50/50 around the $4,350-$4,370 strikes, while Polymarket's September touch contracts for both a $4,300 low and a $4,400 high are priced at roughly 80% likely — consistent with a market that has already swung through much of that range this month and could easily tag either level again before expiry.

Worth flagging for anyone eyeing the gap between platforms: Kalshi's contracts settle on the spot price at one specific moment (5:00 PM ET on the expiry date), while Polymarket's touch contracts pay out if the price crosses the level at any point during the window. A touch contract can look expensive relative to a settle contract on the same strike without being mispriced — it's answering a different question. That structural difference, not a pricing error, is the most likely reason none of today's near-matches cleared the bar for a flagged opportunity.
headline: Gold prediction markets show no arbitrage despite volatile $4,350 price action
